question: What broad category of cellular structure do parasites share with human hosts?
explanation: Parasites are eukaryotic organisms, which means their cells contain a nucleus and organelles similar to human cells. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T1#GNS215_U6_T1_h1)

question: Why is developing drugs against parasites more difficult than creating antibacterial agents?

options.A: Bacterial infections are always easier to diagnose in clinics
options.B: Antiparasitic drugs cannot be administered through oral routes
options.C: Parasites reproduce much faster than human bacterial cells
options.D: Parasitic cells closely resemble human cells in structure

explanation: The similarity between human and parasitic cells makes achieving selective toxicity difficult without harming the host. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T1#GNS215_U6_T1_h1)

question: Mebendazole primarily kills intestinal worms by interfering with which parasite process?
explanation: Benzimidazoles disrupt cellular structures called microtubules, stopping the worm from absorbing glucose and surviving. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T1#GNS215_U6_T1_h2)

question: How does Praziquantel cause the destruction of flatworms and tapeworms?

options.A: By destroying the outer protective cell wall of bacteria
options.B: By blocking folic acid synthesis in the parasite gut
options.C: By stopping the replication of viral genetic material
options.D: By increasing calcium permeability and causing paralysis

explanation: Praziquantel shifts calcium balance inside the worm, inducing tetanic muscle contractions followed by paralysis. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T1#GNS215_U6_T1_h2)

question: What is the current first-line treatment recommendation for uncomplicated falciparum malaria?
explanation: ACTs are recommended globally as the primary treatment to clear parasites quickly and prevent treatment failure. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T1#GNS215_U6_T1_h3)

question: A patient treated for Plasmodium vivax malaria requires which specific drug to prevent future disease relapses from liver hypnozoites?
explanation: Primaquine is uniquely effective at clearing dormant liver-stage parasites responsible for the relapse of vivax malaria. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T1#GNS215_U6_T1_h3)

question: Metronidazole exerts its therapeutic effect against protozoa primarily by damaging which cellular component?
explanation: Metronidazole is reduced inside the organism to reactive intermediates that cause breakage of microbial and protozoal DNA strands. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T1#GNS215_U6_T1_h4)

question: Which instruction is critical for a patient prescribed oral metronidazole for trichomoniasis?

options.A: Stop the prescription immediately when symptoms resolve
options.B: Avoid consuming alcohol during and immediately after therapy
options.C: Expose skin to direct sunlight to activate the drug
options.D: Take the medication exclusively on an empty stomach with milk

explanation: Metronidazole causes a severe disulfiram-like reaction when mixed with alcohol, leading to flushing, nausea, and severe vomiting. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T1#GNS215_U6_T1_h4)

question: Permethrin cream works against scabies mites by disrupting which physiological mechanism?

options.A: Sodium ion channels in nerve membranes
options.B: Cell wall synthesis in the mite exoskeleton
options.C: Folic acid production inside the gut

explanation: Permethrin disrupts voltage-gated sodium channels, leading to paralysis and death of the scabies mite. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T1#GNS215_U6_T1_h5)

question: A patient treated for a scabies infestation asks when skin itching will completely stop. What is the best nursing response?

options.A: New itching indicates a bacterial superinfection has started
options.B: Antihistamines should be stopped immediately to speed up healing
options.C: Itching may persist for several weeks even after the mites are dead
options.D: Continued itching proves the treatment failed and must be repeated

explanation: Post-scabietic pruritus is common due to an ongoing allergic reaction to dead mites and their waste products under the skin. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T1#GNS215_U6_T1_h5)

question: Why is gastrointestinal upset a common side effect for almost all classes of antiparasitic drugs?

options.A: Interference with pancreatic enzyme release in the duodenum
options.B: Local irritation and the systemic breakdown of parasites in the body
options.C: Their primary action on human gastric acid production cells
options.D: The requirement that all these medications be taken without water

explanation: Gastrointestinal symptoms stem from direct mucosal irritation by the drugs and the inflammatory response to dying parasites. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T1#GNS215_U6_T1_h6)

question: Which of the following laboratory parameters should be monitored during prolonged albendazole or mebendazole therapy? (Select the best match)

options.A: Serum creatinine and random blood glucose
options.B: Liver function tests and complete blood count
options.C: Thyroid stimulating hormone and lipid profile

explanation: Prolonged use of benzimidazoles carries a risk of hepatotoxicity and bone marrow suppression, necessitating periodic blood work. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T1#GNS215_U6_T1_h6)
